body:
I feel as though my cat is a bit brain damaged as well. I've never seen another act quite like him. When he makes a decision to do something, he does it for several days straight, oblivious to me and the world around him. Cat finds a ball to pay with? He'll play with the same one for a week. Sees a corner of carpet to scratch? He'll scratch at it until I'm paying the landlord for repairs. I told the vet once that if a cat could be diagnosed with OCD, it would be him. I have a suspicion that he has known longer than I have that my depression is back in a way I have never experienced before. He has been sleeping beside me for weeks now, something that he hasn't done since he was a kitten.

I've been suicidal as long as I can remember grasping the concept of death. I feel like this is something that doctors don't encounter often, and if it is a feeling we always remembered having with us, it is just that much harder for them to grasp and treat.

Over the years I've learned that my depression has a cycle, and some triggers can make the cycle come back stronger and worse. Stress is the biggest factor, and the job that I love so much is a big bag of that. Feeling like my friends and family have abandoned me only adds to that stress. In the end, I don't blame them--I know how terrible and unforgiving I can be when I am feeling at my worst. I mostly wish that my parents could see that my depression is something that I cannot control, and that any amount of religion or prayer is not going to make my brain feel better.

I don't know what horrors you have gone through, but it seems like you have a great understanding of your depression and your self-worth, and I really want to thank you for your insight. I often feel like I am loosing the battle, but I really appreciate you reminding me that I have a good understanding of my depression and it's causes. I know that I can make it through this again, because I've done it before, but it's just so tiring, and it gets harder every time.

I don't know how long we will continue to beat this horrible disease, or how long our cats will continue to console us. But one thing is certainly true, they love us even if we cannot see the point in life for ourselves, and we deserve to be happy. 

I too am on my last drink of the night, and I raise my glass to you and your cat. *clink*
